topic: Exprimer les Attitudes (Expressing Attitudes: Aimer et Détester)

subUnits.title: 3.1 Le Verbe Aimer + l'Infinitif
notes: Le Verbe Aimer + l'Infinitif
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: conjugate the regular verb aimer, and use it with an infinitive to express likes.
Key Concepts:
1. Aimer — A Regular '-ER' Verb:
- Remove '-ER' from 'aimer' to get the STEM 'aim-', then add the ending for each subject.
- j'aime | tu aimes | il/elle aime | nous aimons | vous aimez | ils/elles aiment
2. Aimer + Infinitive — Expressing Liking an Activity:
- 'Aimer' is often followed by an INFINITIVE (the unconjugated, 'dictionary form' of a second verb).
- J'aime aller au cinéma. (I like going to the cinema.)
- Je n'aime pas manger tôt le matin. (I don't like eating early in the morning.)
- NOTE: 'ne...pas' surrounds the conjugated verb 'aime' in negation.
Formula Box:
aimer: j'aime | tu aimes | il/elle aime | nous aimons | vous aimez | ils/elles aiment
stem: aim- + ending | Negation: je n'aime pas + infinitive
Analogy:

Regular '-ER' verbs like aimer are the reliable, standard-sized screws in a French grammar toolbox: once you learn the ONE consistent pattern, you can apply it CONFIDENTLY to hundreds of other regular verbs you will meet later.
Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Forgetting to use the INFINITIVE form of the second verb after 'aimer' — the second verb must NOT be conjugated.
- Applying an IRREGULAR verb pattern (like être's) to 'aimer,' which is a REGULAR -ER verb.

quiz.q: What does 'aimer' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Aimer' means to like or to love.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'aimer' for 'je' (I)?
quiz.explanation: 'J'aime' — note 'je' contracts to 'j'' before a vowel. Stem aim- + -e ending.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'aimer' for 'nous' (we)?
quiz.explanation: 'Nous aimons' — stem aim- + -ons ending for nous.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'aimer' for 'ils/elles' (they)?
quiz.explanation: 'Ils/elles aiment' — stem aim- + -ent ending for ils/elles.

quiz.q: What type of verb is 'aimer'?
opts: A verb with no fixed pattern
quiz.explanation: 'Aimer' is a regular -ER verb — more predictable than être or avoir, following a consistent stem+ending pattern.

quiz.q: What follows 'aimer' when expressing liking an activity?
opts: Nothing; no second verb can follow
An infinitive (the unconjugated form of a second verb)
Only a noun, never a verb
quiz.explanation: When expressing liking an activity, 'aimer' is followed by an INFINITIVE — the second verb stays in its dictionary form.

quiz.q: How would you say 'I like going to the cinema'?
quiz.explanation: 'J'aime' (correctly conjugated) + 'aller' (infinitive). The second verb must be in the infinitive.

quiz.q: How would you say 'I don't like eating early'?
quiz.explanation: Negation wraps the conjugated verb: 'je n'aime pas' — 'manger' stays as infinitive after 'pas.'

quiz.q: Regular '-ER' verbs are compared to ___ in this week's analogy.
opts: tools with no consistent pattern at all
reliable, standard-sized screws in a toolbox
quiz.explanation: One learned pattern (the -ER ending system) unlocks hundreds of regular verbs — like a standard screw fitting hundreds of applications.

quiz.q: To conjugate a regular '-ER' verb, you ___.
opts: always use the infinitive form only
remove '-er' to get the stem, then add the ending for each subject
randomly guess a new form each time
never change the verb at all
quiz.explanation: The rule: remove '-er' to find the stem, then add the correct subject ending (-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent).

subUnits.title: 3.2 Le Verbe Détester + Nom/l'Infinitif
notes: Le Verbe Détester + Nom/l'Infinitif
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: conjugate the regular verb détester, and use it with a noun or infinitive to express dislikes.
Key Concepts:
1. Détester — Exactly the Same Pattern as Aimer:
- je déteste | tu détestes | il/elle déteste | nous détestons | vous détestez | ils/elles détestent
- Same stem principle: remove '-er' → 'détest-' + ending.
2. Détester + Noun OR Infinitive:
- + NOUN: je déteste l'orange (I hate oranges)
- + INFINITIVE: je déteste regarder la télévision (I hate watching television)
- Both aimer and détester can take either a noun or an infinitive after them.
Formula Box:
détester: je déteste | tu détestes | il/elle déteste | nous détestons | vous détestez | ils/elles détestent
détester + noun: je déteste l'orange
détester + infinitive: je déteste regarder la télévision
Analogy:

Learning 'détester' after already mastering 'aimer' is like learning to ride a SECOND bicycle after already learning the first: the frame, pedals, and steering (the -ER pattern) work in EXACTLY the same way — only the meaning differs.
Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Assuming détester needs an ENTIRELY new conjugation pattern — it follows the SAME -ER pattern as aimer.
- Forgetting that détester, like aimer, can be followed by EITHER a noun or an infinitive.
diagramDescriptions: Side-by-side conjugation table: aimer vs. détester highlighting the identical pattern
Sentence examples: détester + noun / détester + infinitive

quiz.q: What does 'détester' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Détester' means to hate or to detest.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'détester' for 'je' (I)?
quiz.explanation: 'Je déteste' — stem détest- + -e ending for je.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'détester' for 'vous' (you)?
quiz.explanation: 'Vous détestez' — stem détest- + -ez ending for vous.

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'détester' for 'ils/elles' (they)?
quiz.explanation: 'Ils/elles détestent' — stem détest- + -ent ending for ils/elles.

quiz.q: Détester follows the same conjugation pattern as which other verb learned this week?
quiz.explanation: 'Détester' follows the IDENTICAL regular -ER pattern as 'aimer' — same endings, different stem.

quiz.q: Détester can be followed by ___.
opts: only a noun, never an infinitive
only an infinitive, never a noun
quiz.explanation: 'Détester' can be followed by either a noun directly (je déteste l'orange) or an infinitive (je déteste regarder la télévision).

quiz.q: How would you say 'I hate watching television'?
quiz.explanation: 'Je déteste' (correct conjugation) + 'regarder' (infinitive). The second verb must stay in the infinitive.

quiz.q: How would you say 'she hates oranges'?
quiz.explanation: 'Elle déteste l'orange' — 'déteste' correctly conjugated for elle (3rd person singular), followed directly by the noun.

quiz.q: This week's analogy compares learning détester after aimer to ___.
opts: learning to ride a second bicycle after already learning the first
an activity with no connection to prior learning
learning a completely unrelated new skill from scratch
quiz.explanation: The -ER pattern (frame/pedals/steering) is identical — only the 'model' (meaning) differs, so learning effort is minimal.

quiz.q: Why is learning détester's conjugation 'nearly effortless' after learning aimer?
opts: Détester has no conjugation at all
Both follow the same regular '-ER' pattern, with only the stem differing
The two verbs are entirely unrelated in structure
French verbs never share any common patterns
quiz.explanation: Same pattern, different stem — the hard work of learning the -ER system is already done.
